name: Half-N Pyramid with Shared Ratcheting Stop
note: Turtle Donchian breakout entry, then the Turtle pyramid's STOP SCHEDULE: a virtual unit is booked every add_n*N beyond the last unit's level (N = ATR at the original entry, frozen), up to max_units, and one shared stop is dragged to (newest unit - stop_n*N), ratcheting only in the favourable direction and freezing once the stack is full. Exit on that stop or on a close through the exit_n channel. The signal contract permits one entry per trade, so the added units are virtual -- the convex position sizing is NOT tested, only the stop geometry it implies.
source: Original Turtle Trading Rules, 'Adding Units' (adds at 1/2 N intervals from the previous unit's fill, max 4 units per market) and 'Stops for Added Units' (all units share one stop, moved up as units are added). Public PDF: https://oxfordstrat.com/coasdfASD32/uploads/2016/01/turtle-rules.pdf
code:
def family_init(ctx):
    """Turtle pyramid geometry, expressed as a stop schedule.

    N = ATR(n_period) frozen at the original entry. The trade tracks a virtual
    stack of units: a new unit is booked every time price trades add_n * N
    beyond the fill of the MOST RECENT unit, up to max_units, and every add
    drags one SHARED stop up to (newest unit's level - stop_n * N). The stop
    only ever ratchets in the favourable direction, so with four units at 0.5N
    spacing and a 2N stop the whole stack sits risk-free.

    HONEST LIMIT: the signal contract is one entry per trade, so the units
    cannot actually be bought -- the convexity of the position size is NOT
    tested here. What is tested is the exit structure: a single stop anchored
    to the last add rather than to the entry or to a fixed trailing distance,
    which stops moving once the stack is full, plus the Turtle exit-channel
    close.
    """
    ctx.dc = ctx.indicator("donchian", period=int(ctx.p.entry_n))
    ctx.dx = ctx.indicator("donchian", period=int(ctx.p.exit_n))
    ctx.N = ctx.indicator("atr", period=int(ctx.p.n_period))
    ctx._py = None


def _base(ctx, i):
    u, l = ctx.dc.upper[i - 1], ctx.dc.lower[i - 1]
    if u is None or l is None:
        return 0
    if ctx.h[i] > u:
        return 1
    if ctx.l[i] < l:
        return -1
    return 0


def signal(ctx, i):
    sig = _base(ctx, i)
    if not ctx.positions:
        ctx._py = None
        return sig

    p = ctx.positions[0]
    d = 1 if p["side"] == "long" else -1
    j = p["entry_i"]
    st = ctx._py
    if st is None or st["ei"] != j:
        n = ctx.N[j]
        if n is None or n <= 0:
            return sig
        s0 = p["entry"] - d * float(ctx.p.stop_n) * n
        st = {"ei": j, "n": n, "last": p["entry"], "units": 1,
              "stop": s0, "dead": False}
        ctx._py = st
        for q in ctx.positions:
            ctx.modify(position=q, stop=s0)

    if sig and sig == -d:
        st["dead"] = True            # the base condition has gone false

    add = float(ctx.p.add_n) * st["n"]
    mx = max(1, int(ctx.p.max_units))
    moved = False
    while st["units"] < mx and not (ctx.p.need_sig and st["dead"]):
        nxt = st["last"] + d * add
        got = (ctx.h[i] >= nxt) if d > 0 else (ctx.l[i] <= nxt)
        if not got:
            break
        st["last"] = nxt
        st["units"] += 1
        cand = nxt - d * float(ctx.p.stop_n) * st["n"]
        if d > 0:
            if cand > st["stop"]:
                st["stop"] = cand
                moved = True
        else:
            if cand < st["stop"]:
                st["stop"] = cand
                moved = True
    if moved:
        for q in ctx.positions:
            ctx.modify(position=q, stop=st["stop"])
    return sig


def exit_signal(ctx, i):
    """The Turtle channel exit: a close through the exit_n extreme."""
    if not ctx.positions:
        return False
    d = 1 if ctx.positions[0]["side"] == "long" else -1
    u, l = ctx.dx.upper[i - 1], ctx.dx.lower[i - 1]
    if u is None or l is None:
        return False
    if d > 0:
        return ctx.c[i] < l
    return ctx.c[i] > u
